# Install Zumungo in about 15 minutes

Two install paths, one Zumungo. Pick the one that fits what you have. After install, an on-device wizard walks you through configuring AI, discovering devices, and mapping your rooms â no accounts, no cloud signup.

## Install Zumungo on your box

Two paths. Pick whichever fits your hardware and comfort level. The result is identical â the same Zumungo, on your LAN, ready for the browser wizard in Step 2.

### Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi image

- Download the latest image: https://cdn.zumungo.com/zumungo-pi-latest.img.xz Copy Download the image (3.3 GB) · SHA-256 checksum Your download has started. The image is 3.3 GB, about 5 minutes on a fast connection and up to half an hour on a slow one. Your browser shows the progress: the download arrow at the top right in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, or the downloads button in Safari. The file is named zumungo-pi-….img.xz . When it finishes, continue with step 2 and flash it with Raspberry Pi Imager. My download has finished

- Flash to a 64 GB microSD card (32 GB works, but leaves little room for a local AI model) with Raspberry Pi Imager (or balenaEtcher ). Both handle .img.xz directly â no need to unzip.

- Enter your WiFi (skip this if using a network cable): after flashing, the card shows up on your computer as a small drive named bootfs . Open it, double-click zumungo-setup.txt , type your WiFi name and password after the = signs, and save. Zumungo removes your password from the card automatically on first boot.

- Insert the card and power on. First boot takes about 22 minutes — the Pi is unpacking Zumungo's full software stack onto the card (grab a coffee). Every boot after that takes about a minute.

- Continue to Step 2 â the Pi advertises itself as zumungo.local on your LAN.

The image includes Raspberry Pi OS and Debian packages, each provided by its own authors under its own license (GPL and LGPL among them) and included unmodified. Their source is published at archive.raspberrypi.com and deb.debian.org , and we will supply the corresponding source for any such component on request, free of charge. The same notice ships on the card as LICENSES.txt ; full details on the Legal page.

### One command, any Linux box

- Run the installer on your box: $ curl -fsSL https://zumungo.com/install.sh | sudo sh Copy

- Wait â 5 to 20 minutes, depending on your connection and whether the installer needs to bring up Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit (if it sees a GPU).

- Continue to Step 2 â the box registers itself as zumungo.local on your LAN.

Destructive to Docker state: the installer wipes existing Docker containers, images, and volumes so it can bring up a clean stack. It prints a full pre-flight summary and asks for explicit y/N confirmation before touching anything.

Not touched: your home directory, apt-installed packages, network/Wi-Fi config, the OS itself.
